reason: Cancel the common q-Pochhammer factors to rewrite R_{a,b,r}(q) as \prod_{i=a+1}^b (1-q^{r+i})/(1-q^i). In the formal power series ring Z[[q]], each factor (1-q^i)^{-1} equals \sum_{m>=0} q^{mi} by the geometric-series identity. Because the product is finite, substituting these inverses yields exactly F_{a,b,r}(q). Hence F is the power-series expansion of R at 0. If R is actually a polynomial, then its formal power-series expansion is the polynomial itself, so all coefficients [q^j] agree with those of F.
